subject: english
question: Identify the incorrect part: 'Neither he (A) / nor his brother (B) / are attending (C) / the wedding (D).'

explanation.simple: When subjects are connected by 'neither... nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject ('his brother', singular). Thus, it should be 'is attending'.
steps: Subject nearer to verb is singular ('his brother').
explanation.exam_tip: Neither... nor: verb follows the subject closest to it.

subject: english
question: Find the error: 'She don't know (A) / the answer (B) / to the question (C) / asked yesterday (D).'

explanation.simple: Third person singular subject ('She') takes 'doesn't' (does not), not 'don't'. Correct: 'She doesn't know'.
explanation.exam_tip: He/She/It takes does/doesn't.

subject: english
question: Identify the error: 'He has visited (A) / Agra (B) / yesterday (C) / with his friends (D).'

explanation.simple: With past time markers like 'yesterday', simple past tense must be used ('visited'), not present perfect ('has visited').

methods.name: Tense with Time Adverbs
steps: Simple past with past point of time.

explanation.exam_tip: Never use present perfect with yesterday, ago, or last year.

subject: english
question: Spot the error: 'The furnitures (A) / in this room (B) / are (C) / very old (D).'

explanation.simple: 'Furniture' is an uncountable noun with no plural form 'furnitures'. It takes a singular verb: 'The furniture in this room is very old'.

methods.name: Uncountable Nouns
steps: Furniture, luggage, scenery, advice are uncountable.

explanation.exam_tip: Words like scenery, furniture, luggage, information are never pluralized.

subject: english
question: Identify the error: 'One of my friend (A) / is an engineer (B) / working (C) / in Germany (D).'

explanation.simple: The structure 'One of the / One of my' is always followed by a plural noun and a singular verb. Correct: 'One of my friends'.

methods.name: 'One of' Rule
steps: One of + plural noun + singular verb.

explanation.exam_tip: One of + plural noun + singular verb. Most repeated SSC rule.

subject: english
question: Spot the error: 'Scarcely had he (A) / left the house (B) / then it began (C) / to rain heavily (D).'

explanation.simple: 'Scarcely' and 'Hardly' are always paired with 'when' or 'before', never with 'then' or 'than'. Correct: 'when it began'.
explanation.exam_tip: Scarcely... when; Hardly... when; No sooner... than.

subject: english
question: Identify the error: 'Each of the girls (A) / have performed (B) / very well (C) / on the stage (D).'

explanation.simple: 'Each of' takes a singular verb. Correct: 'has performed', not 'have performed'.
steps: Each of + Plural Noun + Singular Verb.
explanation.exam_tip: Each, every, either, neither take singular verbs.

subject: english
question: Spot the error: 'The teacher prevented (A) / the boy (B) / from to enter (C) / the classroom (D).'

explanation.simple: The preposition 'from' is followed by a gerund (verb+ing). Correct: 'from entering'.
explanation.exam_tip: Prevent, prohibit, abstain, refrain take 'from + V-ing'.

subject: english
question: Spot the error: 'He is senior (A) / than me (B) / in service (C) / by two years (D).'

explanation.simple: Adjectives ending in '-ior' (senior, junior, prior, superior, inferior) take the preposition 'to', never 'than'. Correct: 'senior to me'.
explanation.exam_tip: Senior, junior, superior, inferior take 'to'.

subject: english
question: Spot the error: 'If I was you, (A) / I would not (B) / accept (C) / this offer (D).'

explanation.simple: In hypothetical subjunctive conditionals, 'were' is used for all persons. Correct: 'If I were you'.
explanation.exam_tip: In unreal conditional clauses, always use 'were' (never 'was').

subject: english
question: Spot the error: 'Although he worked hard, (A) / but he failed (B) / to secure (C) / the top rank (D).'

explanation.simple: 'Although' / 'Though' is followed by 'yet' or a comma, never by 'but'. Correct: 'yet he failed' or simply 'he failed'.
explanation.exam_tip: Never use 'but' after although/though.

subject: english
question: Spot the error: 'Unless you do not work hard (A) / you cannot (B) / pass (C) / the examination (D).'

options.text: Unless you do not work hard

explanation.simple: 'Unless' is already negative and means 'if not'. Using 'do not' creates a double negative. Correct: 'Unless you work hard'.
explanation.exam_tip: Never use 'not' in clauses introduced by unless or until.

subject: english
question: Spot the error: 'The climate of Chennai (A) / is hotter (B) / than Delhi (C) / in summer (D).'

explanation.simple: Comparison must be between equivalent entities. We must compare climate to climate, not climate to a city. Correct: 'than that of Delhi'.

methods.name: Illogical Comparison
steps: than that of (singular) / than those of (plural).

explanation.exam_tip: Use 'that of' (singular) or 'those of' (plural) for comparison of attributes.

subject: english
question: Spot the error: 'No sooner did the bell ring (A) / when the children (B) / rushed out (C) / of the classroom (D).'

options.text: No sooner did the bell ring

explanation.simple: 'No sooner' is always paired with 'than', not 'when'. Correct: 'than the children rushed out'.
explanation.exam_tip: No sooner takes THAN (not when, then, or that).

subject: english
question: Spot the error: 'Being a rainy day, (A) / he decided (B) / to stay (C) / at home (D).'

explanation.simple: This is a dangling/unattached participle. The grammatical subject of the sentence ('he') would improperly become the subject of 'being a rainy day'. Correct: 'It being a rainy day'.
explanation.exam_tip: Always supply 'It being' for weather and time clauses.

subject: english
question: Spot the error: 'He told me (A) / that he is reading (B) / a novel (C) / since morning (D).'

explanation.simple: In indirect speech with a past reporting verb ('told') and a duration marker ('since morning'), past perfect continuous must be used. Correct: 'that he had been reading'.
explanation.exam_tip: 'Since/for' denoting continuing action requires perfect continuous tense.

subject: english
question: Spot the error: 'The captain, as well as (A) / the players, were (B) / present in (C) / the ground (D).'

explanation.simple: When subjects are joined by 'as well as', 'with', 'along with', 'together with', the verb agrees with the FIRST subject ('The captain', singular). Correct: 'was present'.

methods.name: Parenthetical Addition
steps: As well as joins: look at the first subject.

explanation.exam_tip: As well as, along with, with, accompanied by: verb agrees with first subject.

subject: english
question: Spot the error: 'It is high time (A) / that you start (B) / studying seriously (C) / for the exam (D).'

explanation.simple: The phrase 'It is time / It is high time / It is about time' followed by a subject requires the subjunctive Simple Past tense (V2). Correct: 'that you started'.
steps: It is high time + Subject + V2.

methods.name: Idiomatic Past Subjunctive
steps: It is high time you started.

explanation.exam_tip: It is high time + Subject + Simple Past (V2).

subject: english
question: Spot the error: 'Not only he lost (A) / his luggage (B) / but also his wallet (C) / in the journey (D).'

explanation.simple: Parallel structure: 'but also' precedes a noun phrase ('his wallet'), so 'not only' must precede the corresponding noun phrase ('his luggage'). Correct: 'He lost not only his luggage but also his wallet'.
steps: Correct: 'He lost not only his luggage'.

methods.name: Parallel Structure
steps: Not only X but also Y must govern identical parts of speech.

explanation.exam_tip: Not only and but also must be placed before parallel parts of speech.

subject: english
question: Spot the error: 'Hardly had I arrived (A) / at the airport (B) / than the flight took off (C) / without me (D).'

explanation.simple: 'Hardly' takes 'when', not 'than'. Correct: 'when the flight took off'.
explanation.exam_tip: Hardly/Scarcely... when; No sooner... than.
